More specifically, the focal plane (imagine a plane through space where the lens focuses) is tilted from the plane of the film or sensor.

Normally this is undesirable because parts of the resulting image are unfocused, but with the right tilt this miniature effect is created.

Very small aperture creating a very narrow depth of field.

Hmm. Interesting. Strange interactions.

Small apertures actually increase depth of field (with a pinhole camera giving almost infinite DoF).

"Real" tilt shift photography actually uses an adapter (or special lens) that tilts the the focal plane of the lens with respect to the sensor/film. This is commonly used to produce the miniture effect observed here. A "fake" tilt shift effect can also be generated digitally in post production.
